72:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Jinn In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform his people that the jinn listened to the Qur’an, believed in it, accepted it, and submitted to it. God the Almighty says: Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened and said, “Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’an * It guides to the right course, meaning to the right path and success. So we have believed in it, and we will never associate with our Lord anyone. This situation is similar to God the Almighty’s saying: And when We turned to you a group of jinn, listening to the Qur’an. We have already presented the hadiths that have been reported on this subject, so there is no need to repeat them here. God the Almighty said: And that He, the Most High, is the Grandfather of our Lord. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: The Grandfather of our Lord, meaning His action, command, and power. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Grandfather of God’s favors, power, and blessings upon His creation. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah: The majesty of our Lord. Qatadah said: Exalted is His majesty, greatness, and command. As-Suddi said: Exalted is the command of our Lord. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda’, Mujahid, and Ibn Jurayj: Exalted is His mention. Saeed bin Jubair said: Exalted is the Grandfather of our Lord, meaning Exalted is our Lord. As for what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Muqri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A grandfather is a father. If the jinn had known that there was a grandfather among mankind, they would not have said: Exalted is the Grandfather of our Lord. This is a good chain of transmission, but I do not understand the meaning of these words, and perhaps something has been omitted, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: He has not taken a wife or a son means He is exalted above taking a wife or children. That is, the jinn said: The Lord, glory be to Him, was far removed from taking a wife or a son when they submitted to Islam and believed in the Qur’an. Then they said: And that our foolish one used to say about God an outrage. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said: Our foolish one means Iblis. Outrageous. As-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik: Outrageous means unjustly. Ibn Zayd said: That is, great injustice. It is possible that what is meant by their saying our foolish one is a generic name for everyone who claims that God has a wife or a son. For this reason they said: And that our foolish one used to say about God an outrage, that is, before his conversion to Islam. About God an outrage, that is, falsely and deceitfully. For this reason they said: And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never tell a lie about God. That is, we did not think that mankind and the jinn would collude to lie about God, the Most High, by attributing a wife or a son to Him. So when we heard this Qur’an and believed in it, we knew that they They were lying to God about that. God the Almighty said: And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, but they increased them in burden. That is, we used to think that we had superiority over mankind because they used to seek refuge with us when they settled in a valley or a desolate place in the wilderness or elsewhere, just as it was the custom of the Arabs in their pre-Islamic period to seek refuge in the great place of that place from the jinn, lest they be afflicted with something that would harm them, just as one of them would enter the land of his enemies under the protection, covenant, and protection of an important man. So when the jinn saw that mankind sought refuge with them out of fear of them, they increased them in burden, that is, in fear, terror, and panic, until they remained more fearful of them and sought refuge with them more, as Qatada said, so they increased them in burden, that is, in sin, and the jinn became more audacious toward them. Al-Suddi said: A man would go out with his family and come to the land, and he would descend into it and say: I seek refuge in the master of this valley from the jinn, lest I, my wealth, my children, or my livestock be harmed in it. Qatada said: So if he sought refuge with them from someone other than God, the jinn would then inflict harm upon them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan narrated to us, Wahb bin Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Az-Zubayr bin Al-Kharit narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The jinn used to fear humans just as humans feared them, or even more so. When humans would descend into a valley, the jinn would flee, and the chief of the people would say, We seek refuge with the chief of the people of this valley. The jinn would say, We see them fleeing from us just as we flee from them. So they approached the humans and struck them with madness and insanity. This is the meaning of the statement of God, the Almighty: {And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, but they increased them in burden} meaning in sin. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ar-Rabi’ and Zaid bin Aslam said, burden means fear. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so they increased them in burden meaning in sin. Qatadah said the same. Mujahid said: The disbelievers increased in transgression. He sheltered us in a shepherd’s house for the night. When midnight came, a wolf came and took a lamb from the sheep. The shepherd jumped up and said: O Amer, the valley is your neighbor. Then a crier, whom we did not see, called out: O Sarhan, let him go. The lamb came running until it entered the sheep without a single bruise. And God the Almighty revealed to His Messenger in Mecca, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, but they increased them in burden. Then he said: Something similar was narrated from Ubayd ibn Umair, Mujahid, Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Hasan, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ibrahim al-Nakha’i. It may be that this wolf that took the lamb, which is a young sheep, was a jinn in order to terrify and fear the human being, then he returned it to him when he sought refuge with it in order to mislead him, humiliate him, and make him abandon his religion. And God knows best. And His Almighty saying, And that they assumed, as you assumed, that God would not send anyone, meaning that God would not send a messenger after this period, as al-Kalbi and Ibn Jarir said.

They knew that this was the reason for which the heavens were preserved. So those of them who believed believed, and those who remained rebelled in their transgression, as mentioned in the hadith of Ibn Abbas in that regard when he said in Surat Al-Ahqaf, And when We turned to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an [the verse]. There is no doubt that when this happened, which was the abundance of meteors in the sky and the shooting of them, mankind and jinn were terrified and disturbed by it, and they thought that it was for the destruction of the world, as Al-Suddi said: The sky was not guarded unless there was a prophet on the earth or a religion of God was apparent. So they went to him and he smelled it. He said: Your companion is in Mecca. So he sent seven men from the jinn of Nasibin and they went to Mecca and found the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing praying in the Sacred Mosque, reciting the Qur’an. They approached him out of eagerness to recite the Qur’an until their teeth were about to hit him. We have mentioned this chapter in full at the beginning of the mission in the long Book of the Biography, and God knows best, and to God be praise and thanks.
